choice: Electron ^39 as the desktop runtime with Node.js main process and vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript renderer
alternatives: A renderer UI framework such as React
rationale: URS-001 explicitly requires Node.js and Electron, and vanilla web assets satisfy the HTML/CSS requirement without introducing an unrequested framework.

dependency.name: electron
dependency.reason: Provides the required Electron desktop runtime and development launch command.

choice: Run calculator state transitions and arithmetic entirely in the renderer process; use the main process only for window lifecycle
alternatives: Move arithmetic into the main process over IPC
rationale: The calculator has no privileged data or I/O needs, so renderer-local synchronous state transitions minimize complexity and latency while preserving the Electron security boundary.

choice: No IPC or HTTP API for calculator operations; DOM events and internal modules are used
alternatives: Expose calculator operations through Electron IPC
Use preload methods for every button action
rationale: The requirements are local UI interactions and do not require main-process privileges or external clients. Avoiding unnecessary IPC and HTTP surfaces reduces attack surface and contract overhead.

choice: No persistent storage; calculator state is in-memory and reset on application reload
alternatives: Persist state in a JSON file under userData
Persist state through a remote service
rationale: No requirement asks for history, settings, or recovery across launches. Avoiding storage prevents unnecessary sensitive-data retention and migration obligations.

choice: Synchronous in-memory state transitions and arithmetic in renderer event handlers
rationale: All required operations are small and deterministic. Synchronous processing makes display updates immediate and avoids loading, retry, timeout, and duplicate-request concerns.

choice: BrowserWindow uses contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false, and sandbox: true; preload exposes no calculator API
alternatives: Expose calculator operations through a broad preload bridge
rationale: The renderer needs only DOM APIs, so the strongest Electron defaults can be retained without weakening security.

choice: Use Node.js built-in node:test for calculator unit tests and Electron integration tests for the packaged UI; use stable data-testid hooks
rationale: The test strategy verifies pure state transitions quickly and validates the real Electron renderer without adding an unrequested test dependency.

choice: Define package.json scripts for start and test, package the Electron application with local HTML/CSS/JavaScript assets, and inject environment-specific values only through build/launcher configuration
alternatives: Run from an ad hoc source command without package metadata
Bundle a server and external runtime
Store environment secrets in renderer source
rationale: The repository has no existing package manifest or deployment contract. Explicit scripts and local assets make build, pre-deployment validation, and rollback to the prior packaged artifact reproducible. This application has no secrets or environment-specific external integration.

choice: Treat the application as a new system with no legacy IPC, HTTP, or storage contracts; preserve stable UI test identifiers after initial release
alternatives: Introduce compatibility adapters for nonexistent interfaces
Create a versioned storage migration before persistence exists
rationale: The As-Is baseline contains no modules, interfaces, dependencies, tests, or storage. There is nothing to migrate, but UI automation identifiers become the first compatibility surface.
